newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Simsmetal criticises ACCC, says profits OK.
newsitem.headline: Simsmetal criticises ACCC, says profits OK.

text.p: Metal recycler Simsmetal Ltd said on Thursday that the nation's anti-monoplies authority was attempting to create excessive competition but added that its own profit outlook was improving.

The company said earlier that it would not proceed with the planned purchase of the unlisted Wanless Metal Industries Pty Ltd, based in the state of Queensland, due to opposition from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).
Simsmetal managing director John Crabb said the company had other acquisition targets in its sights, but takeovers in Australia had become difficult due to the ACCC's view of the market.

"As far as I am concerned, the ACCC seem intent on creating competition at any cost," said Crabb, who believed there should be consolidation in many industries rather than encouragement for what he called "bit players".
"I think within the global business theatre that quite honestly Australia is at risk of becoming an off-Broadway show."
Simsmetal did not say how much it was prepared to pay for Wanless, which has 80 employees and eight sites in Queensland.
Crabb said the company was examining four to five acquisition candidates locally and overseas, some of which would cost much more than Wanless.

He also said the company still believed its fourth quarter would show an improvement following a weak first nine months which was mainly driven by lower first half demand and prices for secondary ferrous and non ferrous metals.
Simsmetal could also exceed analysts forecasts for the full-year result, he said.
The company was tipped by market analysts to achieve a 1996/97 (July-June) net profit of about A$33 million compared with A$46.7 million a year earlier.
"I think that our fourth quarter will be better and I think that we will be somewhere near the market estimate," Crabb said.
"I think that probably we might even exceed them. But we will do what we said we were going to do, we will have a better fourth quarter."
Simsmetal shares were steady at A$9.20 at 12.50 p.m. (0250 GMT), giving the company a market capitalisation of A$737.53 million based on 80.17 million shares on issue.
